text:
Maya: Quick favor — running a small-batch smoke to validate the continuous-batching change on staging. Can someone run a throughput / p95 check with short sequences and max-batch=6? Posting the current run config below. TL;DR: want to catch any queueing tail/regressions.

Kevin: On it. Which model + tag should I use, and do you want raw traces?

Maya: Use `gpt-small-v1-quant` (q4_16) — model tag `cb-experiments-2026-03`. Loadgen profile: `smoke-shortseq-128`. Yes include traces if possible, but priority is p95 and throughput.

Ryan: I'll kick this off on gpu-pool-3. Note: with seq=128 the KV cache can be pressured if batch > 8, so I'll cap batch to 6 as requested and also set `--max-tokens=512` to be safe.

Sarah: Copy. Also please compare p95 against baseline (master @ 2026-03-09). bench-bot — can you post the baseline numbers for that model/profile?

bench-bot: baseline (master 2026-03-09, smoke-shortseq-128): p50=12ms, p90=26ms, p95=38ms, throughput=420 tok/s.

Kevin: Started run `run-id=cb-smoke-1842590123-k` on gpu-pool-3. Early logs show a queue depth spike around 15s into the run when concurrent inflight requests jump. Pasting snippet:

```
[00:00:14] queue_depth=3 inflight=2 latency=14ms
[00:00:15] queue_depth=12 inflight=10 latency=92ms <-- spike
[00:00:16] queue_depth=4 inflight=3 latency=16ms
```

Kevin: Looks like a transient batching burst. Uploading trace to perf dash at: https://perf.internal.redwood/runs/cb-smoke-1842590123-k

Maya: If we see those spikes, try enabling `cb-adaptive-window=true` and set `queue-timeout-ms=30`. Also for quick mitigation we can fallback to `--max-batch-size=4 --enable-prefix-cache=true`. I've left a note in PR #3849 (core/continuous-batching refactor) — @Sarah can you take a look for anything risky?

Sarah: Will review PR today. For regression checking: add quantile diffs (p50/p90/p95/p99) in the perf dashboard and tag the run `cb-quick-2026-03-19`. If p95 > baseline * 1.15 we consider it a regression and pause rollout.

Kevin: Uploaded the traces and quantile report. Early aggregated numbers: p50=13ms (+1ms), p95=46ms (+8ms, ~1.21x), throughput=405 tok/s (-3.5%). I'll try with adaptive window on.

Maya: Thanks. If regression persists with adaptive window, do the fallback config and reopen the canary. Also add `--kernel-hint=auto` vs `--kernel-hint=legacy` diff to the run metadata (we suspect a kernel selection path may be the culprit).

Ryan: Got it — running 2 more variants: (A) adaptive-window on, max-batch=6; (B) fallback max-batch=4 + prefix-cache. Will post both sets of numbers in ~30m.

Maya: Awesome. If anyone finds a clear cause (kernel mismatch vs queueing), drop the findings here and mention the incident tag `#perf-regression` so SRE can follow. Thanks all.

Kevin: quick note — pinging @Sarah for the PR review reminder.

Sarah: Reviewing now, will comment on the perf-related code paths and follow up with suggested micro-benchmarks to isolate kernel vs batching effects.

Ryan: Results posted: Variant A p95=42ms; Variant B p95=36ms. Variant B (fallback) brought p95 below baseline. Sharing CSV and traces on the perf dash.

Maya: Great — Variant B looks safe. We'll hold rollout and update release notes: "enable cb changes behind feature flag; default to fallback if p95 regress >15%". Follow-ups: Sarah will finalize PR comments, Kevin will close the canary if no other regressions, Ryan will schedule deeper profiling for next week.

Kevin: closing loop once I verify no other regressed models. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
